Growth paths and maturity

Current-company research, October 17, 2026. A transparent set of analyst assumptions, not issuer guidance, a target-price fit or calibrated probabilities.

Choose two different things

  1. Early growth pattern: an immediate fade, the initial growth rate maintained for 3 or 5 years, or individually entered growth rates for years 1–3 or 1–5.
  2. Maturity: year 10, 15 or 20, when the selected flexible path reaches stable growth and begins its terminal-value treatment. For 3 explicit years and maturity at 10, there are 7 fade years. For 5 explicit years and maturity at 20, there are 15 fade years.

The legacy immediate-fade path remains the default with exactly its previous ten-year calculations and constant incremental sales/capital. Existing researched cases and historical freezes are unchanged. The AAOI staged capacity case keeps its documented ten-year schedule. Switching to a flexible profile is deliberate and changes the margin and capital schedule as well as the growth shape.

Why no universal ten-year limit?

Damodaran relates the high-growth period to company size, existing growth and competitive advantages. His firm-valuation chapter includes a Cisco example with six high-growth years followed by six transition years. The familiar five-year high-growth stage plus five-year transition is a modeling pattern, not a universal maximum. The duration still needs a business justification.

  • Damodaran: length of the high-growth period
  • Firm valuation, Illustration 6.3: Cisco
  • Closure in valuation: stable growth and terminal value
These controls implement a simplified, explicit transition. They do not reproduce every Damodaran model. Margin convergence, competitive advantages, capital productivity and risk can evolve on different schedules. Here, growth, margin and capital maturity are synchronized as a stated assumption; WACC is constant throughout, with no capital-structure or risk fade.

Annual growth

Let N be maturity, E be 3 or 5 explicit years, and g be stable growth. Maintained growth uses the initial rate in years 1–E. Annual-entry mode uses the initial scalar in year 1 and the entered rates in years 2–E. Thereafter:

growth(year) = growth(E) + [g − growth(E)] × (year − E) / (N − E)
for year = E+1, …, N

Flexible immediate fade uses initial growth in year 1 and reaches g in year N, using (year − 1)/(N − 1). This follows the original growth timing, but its capital intensity transitions to maturity rather than staying constant. Neither immediate mode nor the explicit phases independently resample each future year.

Margins, reinvestment and terminal consistency

The normalized starting EBIT margin converges linearly to the mature margin over N years. Taxes apply only to positive EBIT; no NOL ledger or automatic loss refund is assumed. WACC is the same scalar in every forecast year and in the terminal formula.

Capital intensity means new capital per unit of new revenue, the reciprocal of incremental sales/capital. It stays at its initial level through E, then transitions linearly to the terminal-consistent endpoint. Flexible immediate mode starts this transition from year zero. No terminal ROIC is inferred from historical accounting ratios, and it is not automatically set equal to WACC.

terminal capital intensity = (1 + g) × mature margin × (1 − tax) / terminal ROIC
fade(year) = max(0, (year − E)/(N − E))
capital intensity(year) = [1 − fade(year)] / initial sales-capital
                       + fade(year) × terminal capital intensity
net reinvestment(year) = max(0, change in revenue × capital intensity(year))
terminal NOPAT = revenue(N) × (1 + g) × mature margin × (1 − tax)
terminal reinvestment = terminal NOPAT × g / terminal ROIC
terminal value at N = (terminal NOPAT − terminal reinvestment) / (WACC − g)

The (1 + g) factor reconciles current-year incremental revenue with the protected engine’s next-year terminal NOPAT timing. With the final forecast year already at stable growth, mature margin and terminal-consistent intensity, FCFF(N) × (1 + g) equals terminal FCFF. A positive mature margin is required to derive finite terminal sales/capital. Stable growth must remain below both WACC and mature marginal ROIC.

The reinvestment total shown in Growth is a modeled net-growth investment requirement. It is not a balance-sheet invested-capital forecast, a maintenance capex schedule or evidence that funding is available. Revenue declines do not automatically release assets. Revenue multiples are shown without inventing future market share.

Monte Carlo and explicit annual paths

Each trial samples one vector: initial growth, mature margin, initial sales/capital and WACC. It then rebuilds the entire annual operating path with the same adapter used by deterministic valuation. For explicit-entry paths, every explicit growth rate shifts by the same percentage-point change between sampled initial growth and baseline initial growth; the fade still ends at fixed stable growth.

trial growth(year) = baseline explicit growth(year)
                  + [sampled initial growth − baseline initial growth]
for explicit years 1–E; then rebuild the fade to g

This is a disclosed parallel-shift path assumption. It is neither independently resampled yearly growth nor fitted economic covariance. Other path shapes require analyst changes to the baseline. The maturity year, explicit phase, tax, stable growth and terminal ROIC stay fixed. WACC is drawn once and constant within that trial. Every explicit annual rate must stay between −50% and 200%; initial growth remains within the existing −50% to 100% scalar bound. Invalid trials are excluded without replacement or clipping, and the exclusions are reported.

Saved work and verification

Existing saved drafts keep their legacy ten-year behavior. New flexible profiles preserve the selected maturity and annual inputs. Malformed flexible saved inputs withhold results instead of being silently filled with research defaults. Loading research explicitly restores its original path; Undo load can restore the prior draft. Path Undo retains independent scalar, notes and claims edits; maturity Undo retains annual-rate edits.

Independent numerical oracles cover the phase and horizon combinations, terminal reinvestment identity, seeded trial replay, invalid annual rates and legacy equivalence. Minimal DOM tests cover the actual input handlers, persistence, Undo, research loading and exports. Static document-renderer previews are layout approximations; authenticated real-browser, touch and screen-reader behavior remains unverified under the existing executor limits.
